Commentary.Commentary: RESUMPTION! Avishka Fernando and Nishan Madushka to open for Lanka. Jayden Seales to bowl first.
...THE CHASE...

UPDATE - 2.35 pm GMT - We have some good news. The game is set to resume at 2.55 pm GMT. The West Indies innings is over and Sri Lanka have to chase 232 runs in 37 overs. So, plenty of cricket still left. Stay tuned.
UPDATE 1426 - The rain has stopped and the umpires are out inspecting! Hopefully we are in for some very good news! Stay tuned.
UPDATE 1412 - Well, we were minutes away from the inspection but the drizzle is back! The insepctiion might be pushed ahead.
UPDATE 1356 GMT - We have some good news! There's an inspection scheduled at 1415 GMT. Let's hope we get news of the game resuming.
UPDATE - 1.26 pm GMT - The rain has stopped once again but we are still unclear about any inspection or any news. Let's hope the rain doesn't interrupt now and we get some action shortly.

UPDATE - 12.55 pm GMT- Well, not the news we were hoping for. It has started to rain once again at Pallekele and the covers are brought back on. So, the waiting game continues and it could also be the end of first innings but we hope for the best. Stay tuned.
UPDATE-12.30 pm GMT - Good news! The rain has stopped and the covers are coming off. The resumption will take some time but optimistic signs at Pallekele. Stay tuned.
UPDATE - 12 pm GMT - It continues to pour down and the whole ground is under cover. There is still a lot of time left in this game but let's hope the rain fades away quickly. Finger's crossed.

UPDATE - 11.31 am GMT - The umpires have had enough and are calling for the covers. The rain has picked up a bit and the players are walking off the field. The whole ground is covered now as the rain has gotten heavier. Stay tuned.

An important phase awaits.

TOSS - West Indies have won the toss and ELECTED TO BAT!

The action now grunts to the 50-over format! West Indies will be facing Lanka in a three game ODI series. The T20 series ended 2-1 in the hosts favour but we did see some exciting games. Let us hope we are in for one here too. Toss and teams in a bit.
... MATCH DAY ...

After three thrilling T20Is, it’s now time for the spotlight to shift to the longer white-ball format! Sri Lanka, with a remarkable comeback after losing the first game, fought back with grit and clinched the T20I series 2-1. Now, they are set to take on West Indies for a three-match ODI series at the Pallekele International Cricket Stadium in Kandy. Despite falling short in the T20Is, West Indies walk into this series with several positives and will be determined to make a stronger impact. On the other hand, Sri Lanka, riding high on momentum, will aim to capitalize early and grab the upper hand. Captain Charith Asalanka leads a formidable squad that will pose a serious challenge to the visitors. The promising Chamindu Wickramasinghe is well on course to make his ODI debut, while Mohamed Shiraz adds depth to the bowling unit, alongside the extra spin option in Dunith Wellalage. Dilshan Madushanka keeps his place in the squad, though Matheesha Pathirana misses out after the T20I series. Sri Lanka’s batting core remains their biggest strength, and if they fire, it will take something special from West Indies to contain them. However, the visitors also have a strong squad at their disposal, with all eyes on Jewel Andrew, the young sensation likely to make his ODI debut. If selected, Andrew could become the youngest-ever ODI debutant for West Indies, a moment of immense pride. Hayden Walsh retains his place in the spin attack alongside Gudakesh Motie, who could play a key role in this series. Alick Athanaze and Keacy Carty bring further balance to the squad, adding depth. Both teams will be eager to strike early and set the tone for the series, making this first encounter a tantalizing contest to watch. With two hungry sides looking for the upper hand, this promises to be a hard-fought, competitive series.
